text: Families order refills and supplies from the store in their client portal. When they call with a question, you need to know what they see.
This is Maria Rivera's portal, and she's logged in.
Logged in is the key. Her saved cards, her pets, member prices and auto-ship only show up after she logs in.
The online pharmacy and store card opens the store.
Products are grouped in these tabs: dental, prescriptions, supplements and gift cards. Featured shows first.
Maria wants joint chews for Maple.
She picks the pet. Every auto-ship belongs to a pet.
Auto-ship is already picked for her, and auto-ship ships free.
Every month is our recommended timing for this one.
Add to cart.
Back to all products.
She also wants dental chews,
for Maple again,
just once, not on auto-ship.
Add to cart.
Now the cart.
Each line shows how it's bought, and which pet it's for.
She can ship, or pick up at an office. Shipping is four ninety-nine today because of the one-time item. The auto-ship renewals ship free.
She confirms the address on file.
She sees the full total, with shipping and tax, before she pays. This is also where a coupon or a gift card goes.
She enters her card.
Saving the card is her choice. The auto-ship will charge this card every month until she cancels.
Place order. Click it once.
The order goes straight to our mail queue, and she gets a receipt by email.
Auto-ship, at the top, lists her auto-ships.
Here are Maple's joint chews, the price, and the next bill date. She can pause or cancel it herself.
And next time she shops, her saved card is ready in the cart.
The most common mistakes: telling a family to check out as a guest when they want their saved card or auto-ship, and promising a member price before they log in.
Remember: saved cards, pets, member prices and auto-ship only show up after the client logs in.
